analysis.title: "There's A Lot Of Fear": Goldman's Pasquariello Puts Himself "On The Dart Board" As Desk Maps The Signposts For A Tactical Bottom
key_insights: Pasquariello says most of the S&P breakdown from the Oct 6 highs through Nov 11 is attributable to NVDA, which shed $2.7tr of market cap over six weeks.
The GS basket of AI leaders is now down on the year after being up 53% YTD five months ago. Pasquariello reads the multiple de-rating as the market pricing AI as a cyclical boom.

Both fundamental and systematic funds have been dumping exposure while option market makers were offsides on gamma and vol. SPX top of book liquidity fell to about $4mm, near YTD lows, adding to realized vol.
Pasquariello says the Fed did not cause the correction, but a tightening cycle does not help and the Fed put is not in play.

Hedge fund positioning has washed out. Fundamental L/S net leverage is 42.3%, the 1st percentile of the past year, and beta-adjusted leverage is 48.2%, a five-year low. CTAs are meaningfully short index futures.

The GS vol Panic Index hit 9.8 of 10 on Friday, and readings above 9.5 have historically signaled near-term relief. In five hiking-regime episodes with panic above 9, subsequent three-month returns averaged just +0.4%.

Broad investor positioning has not washed out. The GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator is at +0.7 and the 75th percentile, versus past buying opportunities at -3.0, -2.6 and -2.5. US equity funds took in nearly $170bn since the start of Q4 and asset manager futures length is in the 82nd percentile.

Friday showed elements of panic: deep S&P vol curve inversion, the highest VXN since COVID, and a surge in ETF volumes. The six-week S&P straddle price more than doubled from 4% to 8.2%, with convexity at panic levels. VXN closed at 45 and VXSMH at 78, an all-time high.
The Q4 2018 analog: the October 2018 panic was followed by another 6.8% decline over three months. Through Thursday the Nasdaq 100 had done 69% of its 2018 drawdown, the S&P 42% and CDX IG 15%.
Snider's three conditions for an S&P bottom are AI earnings confidence news, a dovish Fed signal and a major positioning decline. Only half of the positioning condition is met so far.

Valuation: the S&P went from 22x to 16x, below its 30-year average, and the Nasdaq 100 is at the lowest multiple of the post-COVID era. On trend EPS the multiple is still in the 83rd percentile since 1990.

Pasquariello's call is that the high in volatility has been seen for this episode, though tails are fat. Coppersmith prefers underwriting vol by selling tech puts at levels where the desk would add length.
Asian authorities are intervening: Taiwan banned shorting below the prior close, China cut margin requirements, and South Korea is preparing to deploy its stabilization fund.

tension_points.bull_case: Hedge fund leverage is at a five-year low, the Panic Index is 9.8 and the multiple has de-rated from 22x to 16x. Pasquariello thinks the vol high has been seen.
tension_points.bear_case: Households still hold risk, the sentiment indicator is at +0.7, the Fed is hiking, and Q4 2018 saw another 6.8% decline after panic with credit having done only 15% of its move.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Snider-style bottom needs AI earnings news, a dovish Fed signal and a major positioning decline. A further leg lower with credit repricing would invalidate the bull view.
